answer.one_line: the maker rebate is real, uncapped and exactly computable, but it is worth at most ~62.5 bp of pair turnover and the binding constraint is a residual that loses 3.7x what a matched pair locks, at an observed loss rate of 1.000. The rebate closes about one eighth of the breakeven gap, and at the authorized 1.00 share it closes none of it.

cap_audit.consequence: at p=0.50 the per-contract credit is $0.003125, NOT $0.0031; a cap would have cost 0.8 bp of pair turnover that the venue does not in fact withhold. No cap is applied anywhere in this module.
cap_audit.why: $0.31 is the cent-rounded formula per 100 contracts over 0.43..0.57, not a truncation. Every published row reproduces from theta*C*p*(1-p) with half-even rounding, and the capture contains no cap language. The rebate is UNCAPPED.

is_the_minus_71_7_comparison_legitimate.ground_1_rate_vs_delta: -71.7 is a regime-to-regime MOVE. A rebate rate can only be compared against the LEVEL, -30.4 bp.
is_the_minus_71_7_comparison_legitimate.ground_2_role_mix: even against -30.4 bp the comparison fails. L5's R4 shows fees of -62.1 bp of turnover, which means L5 PAID TAKER FEES on a material share of that turnover. A maker rebate and a taker fee cannot both be earned on the same fill, so the full both-legs-maker 62.5 bp CANNOT be added to a -30.4 bp figure that was produced partly by taker legs. Doing so double-counts the same notional. And an all-maker counterfactual does not hold L5's completion rate fixed: the taker completions are precisely what produced it.
is_the_minus_71_7_comparison_legitimate.what_can_be_said: the two figures can be compared only on an all-maker sub-population with its OWN measured completion rate and its OWN turnover. We do not hold that measurement, so the comparison is NOT MADE here.

rate_vs_delta.finding: -71.7 bp IS A CHANGE, NOT A LEVEL

denominator_reconciliation.the_2x_trap: a pair turns over 2x ONE LEG's notional, but each leg is ~$0.50, so the pair total is still ~$1.00. The 2x applies when converting FROM maker notional (one leg) TO pair turnover, and the rebate_bp_of_FIRST_LEG_MAKER_NOTIONAL column below is roughly 2x the pair-turnover column, exactly as that conversion requires. Comparing the maker-notional column against L5's bp would overstate our compensation ~2x.

observed_region_test.and_at_the_protocol_size: at Stage-6's own 1.00 share the rebate is $0.00 at EVERY price on the venue grid, because the cent floor is 1.61-4.45 shares. So at the size actually authorized, the rebate changes nothing at all and breakeven stays exactly 78.73%.
observed_region_test.question: does any positive region survive using OBSERVED fill, completion and residual values rather than hypothetical perfect fills?
observed_region_test.why: breakeven needs 78.73% matched without the rebate and ~77.2% with it at size; observed is 67.72% with a 95% CI of [65.62%, 69.81%]. The rebate closes about 1.5 of an 11.0 point gap -- roughly one eighth -- and the CI still excludes breakeven by more than 7 points. On L5's own coins the observed fraction is 57.90%, which is worse.

pair_at_par_test.arithmetic: at X=1.00, p=0.50, both legs maker, the pair earns $0.00625 against a $0.00 lock -- 62.5 bp of pair turnover, financed entirely by the rebate. The rebate EXCEEDS the lock for every pair cost above ~0.9938, and is a majority of gross above ~0.9875.
pair_at_par_test.hypothesis: L5's median pair cost 0.9668 with only 46.2% completing <= 0.96 is explained by rebate financing: a pair at $1.00 has ZERO lock but still earns ~62.5 bp of turnover in maker rebate
pair_at_par_test.why_causally_unproven: three reasons. (1) L5's R4 confirmed incentive yield is +163.4 bp of turnover -- 2.6x the 62.5 bp the maker-rebate formula can produce -- so the maker rebate alone does NOT account for L5's compensation; a liquidity-reward program we have no source-confirmed entitlement to supplies the rest. (2) L5's R4 fees are -62.1 bp, so L5 is not all-maker and cannot be earning the full both-legs-maker rate. (3) The pair-cost distribution SPREAD rather than shifted (median fell 0.9764 -> 0.9609 while p90 rose 1.1705 -> 1.2175), which a pure rebate-financing story does not predict.

what_changes_when_the_rebate_is_credited: THE PAIR GATE'S CONSERVATISM IS QUANTIFIED, AND IT IS LARGE. S6P prices BOTH post-only legs at the TAKER coefficient and counts the rebate as zero. At p1=0.60 with a complement of 0.36 the taker-on-both-legs charge is $0.0327 per contract, taking that pair to $0.9927 and FAILING the gate. The highest complement that clears is 0.32, so the $0.96 ceiling becomes a RAW-price ceiling of $0.92 -- four cents tighter. Priced as what the legs actually are -- two maker fills -- the same pair would instead RECEIVE a rebate. The swing between the two pricings is the schedule's full maker-to-taker spread.

THE CONSERVATISM IS NOT WHAT KILLS IT. Removing the gate's taker pricing entirely and crediting the full both-legs-maker rebate at a size above the cent floor still leaves breakeven at ~77.2% against an observed 67.72%. So S6P's conservatism costs real headroom but is NOT the binding constraint -- the residual is.

ONE TAKER LEG ENDS THE DISCUSSION. At p=0.50 a taker completion costs $0.02 per contract -- 200.0 bp of pair turnover -- against a both-legs-maker credit of 62.5 bp. A single taker leg is worth about 2.8x the entire maker rebate, with the opposite sign.
what_does_not_change: THE VERDICT. Breakeven needs 78.73% matched; observed is 67.72% [65.62%, 69.81%]. Crediting the rebate where the formula and account history support it moves breakeven to ~77.2% AT SIZE and NOT AT ALL at the protocol's 1.00 share. UNECONOMIC either way.

THE REBATE AT THE AUTHORIZED SIZE. $0.00, structurally, at every price. bounds.REBATE_CENT_FLOOR_SHARES = 1.62 and FIRST_LEG_QTY = 1.00, so the protocol sits BELOW its own documented cent floor. S6P's zero-rebate treatment is not merely conservative here -- it is EXACTLY RIGHT.
THE RESIDUAL. Loss rate 1.000 over 7,148 provable residuals, mean -$0.27742 against a +$0.07496 matched lock -- 3.7x. No rebate at any size on the venue grid is of that order of magnitude.
THE EVIDENCE BASE. 95.58% of first legs are UNKNOWABLE under the strict standard. Rebate arithmetic does not touch that.
